About Community Options Australia

Community Options Australia (COA) believes every person deserves to feel understood, supported and confident as they navigate their care journey.
Established in 1996 as a not-for-profit, COA has delivered innovative, person-centred care solutions for older people, people with disability, their families and carers for almost 30 years. Today they are a leader in aged care assessments, including the new Single Assessment System. Relationships are the cornerstone of their work, guided by values of integrity, excellence and respect, and a commitment to helping people flourish.

The Role

Reporting directly to the CEO, this newly created role is one of three Executive Lead appointments as COA builds a new Executive Leadership Team. Alongside accountability for financial management, controls and reporting (with day-to-day accounting and payroll supported by an external partner), the heart of the role is business intelligence, utilisation, growth and enterprise risk.

This role offers the opportunity to shape a more forward-looking approach to finance and performance at COA. While maintaining strong financial stewardship, the focus will be on building the insight, data and commercial discipline that allow the organisation to understand its performance today and plan confidently for what comes next. You will strengthen financial and performance reporting, develop greater visibility of demand, utilisation and workforce capacity, and turn operational and financial data into practical insight for the CEO, Board and Executive Leadership Team. Importantly, you will help COA understand where it can improve performance, strengthen its position within the current contract and pursue sustainable opportunities for future
growth.

The Candidate Profile

COA is seeking a curious, analytical leader who loves data and is energised by what it reveals. The ideal candidate turns numbers into clear insight and recommendations, takes a fit-for-purpose approach to risk, and works as a genuine collaborator alongside the ELT, not off to the side.

The ideal candidate will bring significant senior financial leadership experience across strategy, budgeting, forecasting, reporting and controls, together with strength in business intelligence, utilisation or capacity planning within a service delivery environment. Experience managing government-funded contracts, enterprise risk frameworks, and business development or tendering is essential, as is confident use of Salesforce, Power BI and Xero. A tertiary qualification in accounting, finance or commerce, with CPA, CA or equivalent membership, is required.

Experience in aged care will be highly regarded; however, candidates from health, disability, community services, consulting or other adjacent sectors are encouraged to apply. Most importantly, the successful candidate will share COA's values and a commitment to the older people at the centre of everything they do.

Candidates may be based anywhere along the eastern seaboard, with flexibility to travel to Sydney as required.

Common Equity NSW is a not-for-profit company and registered Community Housing Provider working with 31 community housing co-operatives across NSW, together managing more than 500 dwellings in metropolitan and regional communities.
  
As momentum builds for co-operative housing and new projects come online, Common Equity is focused on strengthening its systems, supporting sustainable growth and delivering positive outcomes for members and communities.

Reporting to the CEO and working as part of the senior leadership team, the Head of Finance and Corporate Services leads finance, technology, data, people and culture, risk, compliance and governance functions.   • Developing financial and growth modelling to support future housing opportunities
  • Implementing AI and data governance frameworks
  • Building on established risk, compliance and governance practices

This is a permanent, full-time role based in Sydney with a hybrid work model, including two days per week in the CBD office. Board and committee meetings are held in person on Tuesday evenings on a rotating monthly basis.

Varuna, The National Writers' House is Australia's leading organisation dedicated to the development of writers and writing. For more than three decades, Varuna has supported Australian writers through prestigious residencies, professional development programs, fellowships and creative opportunities that have helped shape the nation's literary landscape.

Varuna is also the proud presenter of the Blue Mountains Writers' Festival, one of Australia's most vibrant and inclusive literary festivals, alongside a growing year-round public program that connects writers and audiences through ideas, storytelling and creativity.

With a strong reputation, expanding national profile, growing philanthropic relationships and significant recent investment in facilities and programs, Varuna is entering an exciting new phase of its evolution.

The Role 

Reporting to the Chair and Board, the Executive Director will provide strategic and operational leadership to ensure Varuna remains sustainable, influential and well positioned for its next chapter.

This is a rare opportunity to lead one of Australia's most respected literary institutions at a pivotal moment of growth, succession and strategic opportunity. Building on a decade of stable leadership, you will guide organisational strategy, drive financial sustainability, strengthen fundraising and partnerships, and support the continued growth of Varuna's national profile and impact. Working closely with the Board, Creative Director and staff team, you will help define the organisation's future while honouring the values and purpose that sit at its heart.

The Candidate Profile 

Varuna is seeking a collaborative, values-led leader who is excited by the opportunity to steward a nationally significant cultural institution through its next chapter of growth and evolution.

You may already be leading an organisation, division or significant portfolio, or be ready to step into your first Executive Director role. What matters most is your ability to build strong relationships, inspire confidence, navigate complexity and bring people together around a shared purpose.

You will bring experience in organisational leadership, stakeholder engagement and financial stewardship, together with the ability to work effectively with Boards, funders, partners and communities. Exposure to fundraising, philanthropy, partnerships or revenue generation will be highly regarded.

While experience in literature, publishing, arts or culture would be advantageous, we welcome candidates from adjacent sectors who bring a genuine appreciation for creativity, storytelling and the important role cultural institutions play in Australian life.

Most importantly, you will be motivated by the opportunity to help shape Varuna's future while preserving the culture of care, generosity and artistic excellence that has made the organisation so highly regarded within Australia's literary community.

job.title: Philanthropy Manager - Odyssey House
job.description:
What makes Odyssey House special

For almost 50 years, Odyssey House NSW has been transforming lives through evidence-based treatment, recovery and support services for individuals, families and communities impacted by alcohol and other drug dependence.

With a strong reputation for innovation and impact, Odyssey House supports thousands of people each year through residential rehabilitation, community programs, family support services and youth initiatives. At the heart of everything they do is a commitment to creating positive, long-term change and helping people build healthier futures.

As the organisation approaches its 50th anniversary and enters the next phase of a successful capital campaign, this is an exciting opportunity to join a purpose-driven organisation with ambitious plans for growth and impact.
  
Drive philanthropy that changes lives

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced relationship fundraiser to take ownership of an established philanthropy portfolio, and be part of a capital campaign.

As Philanthropy Manager, you will lead major donor, trusts & foundations, PAF and corporate partnership fundraising, working closely with supporters who are passionate about creating meaningful social change.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Communications & Fundraising and sitting within the fundraising leadership team, you'll be responsible for managing sophisticated donor relationships, securing significant philanthropic investment and driving best-practice donor stewardship and moves management.

You'll inherit a strong portfolio including major donors, highly engaged supporters and an established philanthropic program, while also helping shape the next stage of growth as Odyssey House aims to significantly increase fundraising income over the coming years.

This role is perfect for a confident relationship fundraiser who thrives on building connections, making strategic asks and delivering outstanding donor experiences to create lasting impact for the people it helps.

How you'll make a difference
  • Manage and grow a portfolio of major donors, trusts & foundations, PAFs and corporate partners through strategic cultivation, solicitation and stewardship.
  • Develop and implement donor engagement strategies, tailored funding proposals and stewardship plans that strengthen donor retention and lifetime value.
  • Build and manage a strong pipeline of philanthropic opportunities, identifying new prospects and funding partnerships.
  • Prepare compelling grant applications, donor communications, impact reports and funding proposals.
  • Support the delivery and ongoing success of Odyssey House's capital campaign through donor engagement and stewardship activities.
  • Lead fundraising forecasting, income reporting, budgeting and pipeline management activities.
  • Manage and mentor the Database Administrator while supporting best-practice donor management processes.
  • Collaborate across fundraising, communications, finance and operational teams to maximise fundraising outcomes and organisational impact.
  
You're the perfect person if

You're a strategic and relationship-focused fundraiser who enjoys engaging with donors, understanding their motivations and connecting them to meaningful opportunities for impact.

You combine strong emotional intelligence with commercial acumen and are confident managing high-value fundraising conversations while maintaining a donor-centred approach.

To be successful, you will bring:
  • Demonstrated success in high value fundraising (major gifts, trusts & foundations, philanthropy or corporate partnerships).
  • Proven experience with strategic moves management of prospecting, cultivating, asking and stewarding donors.
  • Experience managing fundraising pipelines, revenue targets, budgets and forecasting.
  • High-level written communication skills, including proposal and grant writing.
  • CRM experience, ideally with Raiser's Edge, Blackbaud, Salesforce or similar donor management systems.
  • Confidence conducting donor meetings and making funding asks.
  • Strong reporting, analytical and data management capabilities.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills.
  • The ability to work autonomously while contributing positively to a collaborative team culture.
Experience within higher education, health, social services, community organisations, capital campaigns, gifts in wills, marketing or communications will be highly regarded.
  
Why you'll love working here
  • Join a respected organisation approaching a significant milestone anniversary and period of growth.
  • Lead and grow an established philanthropy portfolio with significant future potential.
  • Contribute to a successful capital campaign already delivering strong results.
  • Work alongside an experienced and supportive leadership team that values collaboration and continuous learning.
  • Enjoy a warm, down-to-earth culture where fundraising, communications and marketing work closely together.
  • Access flexible hybrid working arrangements and NFP salary packaging benefits.
  • Build meaningful relationships with donors who are genuinely invested in changing lives.
  • Play a vital role in helping individuals, families and communities affected by alcohol and other drug dependence.
